This module applies the same saved NIST excerpt the first two modules introduced — no new
source was independently fetched, since the new content here is application (building the
selected control families and assessing them independently), not new citation. The links below
were checked at the time this page was written.

- **[NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, "Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and
  Organizations"](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-37r2.pdf)**
  (PDF, final, December 2018) — the document behind both quotes in this lesson (Implement's and
  Assess's one-line actions), via the same saved excerpt in `sources/nist/` used in the first two
  modules. Curl-checked directly from this session: returns HTTP 200.

- **[Categorize and Select Controls](../categorize-and-select-controls/index.qmd)** — the
  previous module: where the eQMS was categorized moderate-impact and the three control families
  built here (account and identity management, audit, physical and environmental protection) were
  selected and tailored.

- **[Designing an Internal Audit Program](../../fda-and-aabb-in-practice/designing-an-internal-audit-program/index.qmd)** —
  the module that first established, in Lakeshore's own worded rule, that an auditor can't check
  their own work. This module applies that same independence principle to an RMF control
  assessment instead of an internal audit.

- **[The 6 Tasks in the ASSESS Step of the NIST RMF](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NiUDG8f6M1g)**
  (Denise Tawwab, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. An independent
  RMF educator walking through the Assess step's tasks. Third-party training content, not NIST, and
  federal-focused rather than blood-establishment-specific. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed
  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST RMF: Assess Step](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf/assess-step)**
  — NIST's own overview page for the step this lesson's second half applies, including its
  pointers to SP 800-53A. Read it to see the step described by its author. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST RMF: Implement Step](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf/implement-step)**
  — the matching official page for Implement, including the documentation half this lesson stresses.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-53A Rev. 5, publication page](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/a/r5/final)**
  — the NIST guide on how controls are assessed (assessment procedures and methods). Not quoted in
  this lesson; read it to see what a formal assessor's procedures look like beyond the one-line
  Assess action. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-53A Rev. 5 (PDF)](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-53Ar5.pdf)**
  — the full text of the same guide, for anyone who wants the procedures themselves. Not saved
  under `sources/`, so nothing in the lesson depends on it. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST RMF Quick Start Guide: Assess Step FAQs](https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/risk-management/documents/05-Assess%20Step/NIST%20RMF%20Assess%20Step-FAQs.pdf)**
  — a short NIST FAQ on what gets assessed, when, and what follows, including the assessment
  report. Useful as a plain-language companion to the Quality Analyst's assessment. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST RMF: Assessment Cases overview](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf/assess-step/assessment-cases-overview)**
  — NIST's page on worked assessment cases, showing how depth and coverage of an assessment are
  described. A deeper look than this lesson needs. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about implementing and independently assessing controls.

- **[Assessing Security Controls: Keystone of the Risk Management Framework](https://www.isaca.org/resources/isaca-journal/issues/2016/volume-6/assessing-security-controls-keystone-of-the-risk-management-framework)** (ISACA Journal, 2016) — an auditor-minded article on why controls must be tested and retested with results recorded. Dated but the logic matches this lesson's "evidence, not assertion" theme. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Security Assessment and Testing MindMap (1 of 3) | CISSP Domain 6](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A-aNmhB_WjM)** (Destination Certification, YouTube) — a compact overview of assessment and testing concepts: audits, scans, reviews and who should perform them. CISSP Domain 6 (Security Assessment and Testing). Verified via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[CISSP Domain 6 Guide: Security Testing Explained](https://www.readynez.com/us/blog/beyond-vulnerability-scans-a-guide-to-cissp-domain-6/)** (Readynez, commercial training provider) — a written walk through the kinds of testing and assessment in Domain 6 and how they differ in the evidence they produce. Vendor content. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
